profiles.name: Cody Beau Porter
profiles.description: In July 2020 in Portland, OR, Cody Beau Porter, 28, was charged with forcibly interfering with a federal officer for allegedly assaulting officers with a high-intensity laser during a protest related to police brutality and the murder of George Floyd. Case dismissed as part of a deferred resolution agreement.
profiles.finding: Court protest-case list corroborates case; no verified portrait.

profiles.name: Cody Nowlin
profiles.description: Cody Nowlin is one of the four Little Rock, Arkansas defendants — alongside Mujera Benjamin Lunga’ho, Renea Goddard, and Angel Espinosa-Villegas — federally prosecuted for the torching of Little Rock police vehicles during the protests that followed the police murder of George Floyd. In September 2022 he pleaded guilty to possession of a Molotov cocktail and was sentenced to 18 months in federal prison. He began his sentence in 2024.
profiles.finding: Possible conflated identity: reporting names Emily Nowlin and prosecutor Cody Hiland, not Cody Nowlin. Flag identity review; reject model/baseball/NAVSUP namesakes.

profiles.name: Craig Michael Digangi
profiles.description: Craig Michael Digangi, 27, of Erie, PA was sentenced to 16-36 months in state prison after pleading guilty to felony rioting and two misdemeanors for participation in the May 2020 Black Lives Matter protests in Erie. He is accused of throwing bricks at — and injuring — officers in the 500 block of State Street and smashing tables outside the Ember and Forge coffee shop.
profiles.finding: Erie obituary names son Craig but supplies no verified subject portrait.

profiles.name: Darion Lindsey
profiles.description: Darion Lindsey, 19, was charged with arson after allegedly setting fire to a Chicago Transit Authority van during a 2020 protest in response to the death of George Floyd. Sentenced to 38 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: DOJ complaint corroborates case; hospital namesake unlinked.

profiles.name: David Bermudez
profiles.description: On March 24, 2022 David Bermudez, 33, of Los Angeles, CA pled "no contest" to a charge of looting. Bermudez was arrested in Los Angeles by the Safe LA Task Force after the George Floyd Protests. Sentenced to 2 years in county jail.
profiles.finding: Florida/South Carolina booking namesakes and older graffiti cleaner unlinked.

profiles.name: Denzal Stewart
profiles.description: Denzal Stewart, 24, was charged with arson after allegedly setting fire to a Chicago Transit Authority van during a 2020 protest in response to the death of George Floyd. Sentenced to 45 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Sun-Times action image names two defendants; subject identification and usable crop pending.

profiles.name: Devarian Haynes
profiles.description: Devarian Haynes, 23, of Las Vegas was charged with co-defendants Tyree Walker and Ricardo Densmore for conspiracy to commit arson and arson after a May 30, 2020 video showed Walker and Haynes setting a police car on fire during protests over the death of George Floyd. Sentenced to 24 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: KTNV case coverage; later Harris County booking lead requires independent identity connection.

profiles.name: Devon Bryce Poland
profiles.description: Devon Bryce Poland, 22, was charged in Cleveland, OH with co-defendant Brandon Michael Althof Long for the same conspiracy — they traveled from PA to participate in Cleveland riots with a vehicle containing a hammer, fire-starters, a glass liquor bottle, and a Glock. Case dismissed March 2021.
profiles.finding: Official case list only; no verified portrait.

profiles.name: Devon Vaughn
profiles.description: Devon Vaughn, 23, was indicted on July 7, 2021 for setting fire to a furniture store at a Kenosha, WI protest in 2020. Sentenced to 40 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Wisconsin Right Now group case report; other wanted-suspect images must not be assigned to Vaughn.

profiles.name: Dominic D. Brown
profiles.description: Dominic D. Brown, 18, of Knoxville, TN was charged with riots and civil disorder after posting profane Snapchat messages calling for a riot and after he was observed picking up a trash can lid filled with an unclear liquid and striking an officer who was sitting in a vehicle. Sentenced to 24 months federal prison plus a $100 fine.
profiles.finding: WVLT explicitly captions Dominic Brown and credits Knox County Sheriff; age18, Knoxville2020 incident matches DOJ. Original800x450 retained with publisher blurred sidebars.

profiles.name: Dontario J. Stephens
profiles.description: Dontario J. Stephens, 27, of Tampa, FL was charged with grand theft and burglary during a state of emergency following his participation in a Black Lives Matter protest over Memorial Day weekend 2020. Stephens allegedly took $50,000 worth of property from a local Gold N Diamond store. Pled guilty to reduced charges; sentenced to 13 months in Florida state prison.
profiles.finding: Third-party 2025 booking exact name requires original sheriff source and case linkage.

profiles.name: Dyshika McFadden
profiles.description: Dyshika McFadden, Miguel Ramos, and Tindal are accused of using an aerosol can and open flame to set fire to a Rochester PD vehicle during May 30, 2020 demonstrations in Rochester, NY in response to the death of George Floyd. The car was destroyed; the burning was broadcast on Facebook Live in real-time. Sentenced to 30 months federal prison plus 3 years supervised release and $4,287 restitution.
profiles.finding: Rochester case reporting found; author image is not defendant.

profiles.name: Earlja Dudley
profiles.description:
Attempted arson of a Trenton police vehicle (2020, federal civil disorder). Sentence: 30 months federal prison. Verified via public court/press records: https://www.justice.gov/usao-nj/pr/mercer-county-man-sentenced-30-months-prison-interfering-law-enforcement-officers-during

Earlja J. Dudley, 27, was charged with attempt to damage government property by fire and attempt to damage property in commerce by fire on June 17, 2020 for setting a Trenton Police vehicle on fire on May 31, 2020. Dudley was identified through bystander video showing him placing a burning object into the engine well of the vehicle and moving away, plus publicly posted social media photos. Sentenced to 30 months federal prison plus 3 years supervised release.
profiles.finding: Complaint and DailyVoice tag corroborate case; portrait unresolved.

profiles.name: Felix Missael Alva
profiles.description: On May 30, 2020 a Denver detective working downtown saw a white Jeep stop nearby with a male passenger producing a black semi-automatic handgun and saying "This ain't no peaceful protest" before firing approximately 6-10 rounds into the air while a DPD helicopter and a news helicopter were overhead. Felix Missael Alva, 29, was identified as the shooter; an Aurora SWAT search of his residence found firearms in a shed. Alva was a previously deported foreign national. Sentenced to 24 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: DOJ Denver case corroboration; no verified portrait.

profiles.name: Gabriela Brigitte Jimenez
profiles.description: On March 24, 2022 Gabriela Brigitte Jimenez, 33, of Los Angeles, CA pled "no contest" to a charge of looting. She was arrested in Los Angeles by the "Safe LA Task Force" after the George Floyd Protests. Sentenced to 1 day in county jail.
profiles.finding: Unrelated viral Gabriela Rico Jimenez excluded; no verified portrait.

profiles.name: Jeanette Renee Wallace
profiles.description: Jeanette Wallace, 24, was charged with depredation against U.S. property after the May 30, 2020 protest in Las Vegas, NV (initially decrying George Floyd's death) turned tense. Some demonstrators vandalized buildings and threw bottles, fireworks, and rocks at officers in riot gear; later some gathered at the federal building, kicking and throwing items to gain entry. A federal security guard was threatened. Damage exceeded $70,000. Wallace was identified via facial recognition and Facebook. Sentenced to 36 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Las Vegas Sun case corroboration; legislator, ambassador, obituary and CEO namesakes excluded.

profiles.name: Jessica Lynn White
profiles.description: Jessica Lynn White, 33, was arrested with co-defendant Matthew Scott White in connection with a fire set at an Enterprise Rent-A-Car building in St. Paul, MN on May 28, 2020. Surveillance video showed her standing outside while Matthew White entered the building; flames were visible behind him as he exited. Case dismissed.
profiles.finding: ATF case list; model, Detroit victim, Florida booking and provider namesakes excluded.

profiles.name: John Michael Santiago
profiles.description: During 2020 protests in Rochester, NY over the killing of Daniel Prude, John Michael Santiago, 24, threw fireworks at police officers and participated in blockading. He was arrested later for civil disorder; while in custody he assaulted two corrections officers. Sentenced to 33 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Rochester case query; astronomy student and other namesakes unlinked.

profiles.name: Julian Renee Mejia
profiles.description: On September 10, 2020 Julian Renee Mejia, 35, of Los Angeles, CA pled "no contest" to a charge of looting. He was arrested in Los Angeles by the "Safe LA Task Force" after the George Floyd Protests. Sentenced to 12 months county jail.
profiles.finding: Exact name and LA looting queries yielded no verified portrait.

profiles.name: Kadeem A. Dockery
profiles.description: On May 31, 2020 following protests in Trenton, NJ, Kadeem Dockery, 29, threw an explosive device through the open driver's window of a police car. While Justin Spry was being arrested, Dockery lit an explosive device and threw it at the arresting officers, which exploded at their feet. Sentenced to 27 months federal prison plus 3 years supervised release.
profiles.finding: AP sentencing corroboration; original image source unresolved.
